fields.contract: Borrowed IOnlineSubsystem pointer. Null subsystem prevents both support and group+0x1d0 helper allocation.

Strong thread-safe shared pointer pair, copied from setup argument +0x38/+0x40; addref on copy, release on destruction. 0x1410ff0c0 uses this interface when non-null, otherwise obtains a shared interface from subsystem via 0x140d11c90. Exact interface spelling and full API remain unresolved.
Owned FString deep-copied from setup argument +0x48; empty string causes 0x1410fb770 to query the selected interface virtual slot +0x50 for a fallback string; a nonempty string overrides that result.

FSoftObjectPtr, default constructed; consists of weak index/serial +0x28/+0x2c, cached tag +0x30, padding +0x34, FSoftObjectPath FName +0x38 and FString +0x40. 0x141110010 sets it from a UObject or resets it; 0x1410ff760 and 0x1410ff860 resolve with weak pointer and tag caching. FSoftObjectPtr source ownership frees its subpath string.

Borrowed FTimerManager*: initially null, overwritten by argument 3 of 0x141110010 and returned alongside the resolved UObject by 0x1410ff760. 0x1410ff860 returns this manager when the soft object resolves; otherwise finds the game world and returns its FTimerManager, or null when no world exists.

lifecycle: 0x141104600 allocates 0x58 support, initializes all semantic fields and publishes to group+0x110, then allocates distinct 0x48 helper at group+0x1d0 with non-owning support pointer +0x40.

0x1410ed9b0 frees support soft-path and override FString allocations, releases shared controller atomically, then frees support; subsequently destroys helper and frees it. Helper cleanup must not dereference its stale support pointer.
0x141e6b3f0 initializes setup argument shared interface and string to null/empty on this observed game-instance path. Preserve general setup arguments because constructor explicitly copies them.
proposal: Use a noncopyable, group-owned native support struct with borrowed IOnlineSubsystem*, TSharedPtr<actual-interface, ESPMode::ThreadSafe>, FString, FSoftObjectPtr and FTimerManager*. Use real engine types and normal construction/destruction; do not hand-roll weak or ref-count state. Represent helper separately with non-owning pointer and original cleanup order.

Implement exact game-service getter, concrete URL, header, object-construction and registration operations, plus the soft-object setter/getters and timer-manager fallback before promoting support as behaviorally complete. Preserve override and non-editor game-world semantics.
No binary-layout assumption should be made for Linux if source types differ in ABI; preserve source semantics and check platform layout only where binary interoperation requires it.
limitations: Offset 0x34 is alignment padding, not initialized state.
Probe of offset +0x110 alone includes unrelated classes; only identified consumers with matching downstream soft-pointer or support use are attributed here.

Concrete +0x50 URL getter is obscured by anomalous thunk. The +0xc0 constructed object and manager registration need further recovery; implementing an empty operation would omit state. Correlation and user-agent provider implementations are also not yet closed.

steps: Resolve FSoftObjectPtr; any valid UObject suffices (class check is UObject::StaticClass). If valid, return the stored FTimerManager* even if null.
Otherwise invoke subsystem vslot +0x18 for GetInstanceName; 0x140d934b0 ignores the name in this build, returns null unless GEngine is a UGameEngine, then invokes UGameEngine::GetGameWorld().

UGameEngine::GetGameWorld() selects the first Game world context with a world. If present, return &World->GetTimerManager(): its owning game instance manager if present, otherwise its own timer manager. If no world, return null.
Consumers invoke SetTimer and SetTimerForNextTick on the returned pointer (0x1446278d0/0x144627d90 carry matching STAT_SetTimer and STAT_SetTimerForNextTick strings).

shared_interface_operations.selection: 0x1410ff0c0 returns the explicit thread-safe override when its object pointer is nonnull; otherwise it calls 0x140d11c90, copies a thread-safe subsystem-owned shared pointer from subsystem +0x2e8/+0x2f0 only if object exists and its byte +0x10 is nonzero; otherwise returns null. Getter temporarily increments and releases strong counts; the raw result remains dependent on owner lifetime.

observed_virtual_operations.+0x50: Concrete target 0x140a468c0 is an anomalous thunk in this captured Ghidra image and its body is not closed. Caller 0x1410fb770 expects an FString URL base.
observed_virtual_operations.+0x90: Concrete 0x140a6d1c0 tests X-Epic-Correlation-ID and User-Agent independently, sets only missing/empty values using correlation ID provider and service vslot +0xe0 respectively; nonempty headers are preserved.
observed_virtual_operations.+0xc0: Concrete 0x140a28eb0 calls 0x140cfec80, which calls 0x140c7ca20 on subsystem +0x5b0, constructing 0xd8-byte object with service state, returning a newly owned shared pointer pair, and registering the shared object into manager +0x38. Full constructor/registration effects are open.

shared_interface_operations.caveat: The subsystem getter is a concrete direct offset access, not a confirmed standard IOnlineSubsystem getter. A neutral interface must preserve each actual operation; an empty marker type does not close call sites.
shared_interface_operations.identity: The concrete subsystem initializes +0x2e8/+0x2f0 with a game-service MCP object via 0x140a12b80, supplying errors.com.epicgames.oss.gameservicemcp as an error namespace. Constructor installs vtable 0x145aaa118; a neutral MCP game-service abstraction is defensible.
